primary_sources.producer: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Geographer; government study with reproduced1960 treaty text, archived at FSU
primary_sources.title: International Boundary Study42: Burma–China
primary_sources.targeted_locator: Printed14–15, ArticleVII paragraph2(7), specifically MongKo/NamKo original-course, NamHkai/NamPangWa, ManHsing/NamHpawn and Nu junction sequence.
primary_sources.finding: The treaty text names an ordered southern-sector river/pass route. For MongKo/NamKo it expressly references the course at past demarcation. It then follows NamHkai/NamPangWa and ManHsing/NamHpawn to the Nu, then Nu to TiKaiKou/NanMen. This gives a concrete named-reach map lead rather than a generic country-wide map request.
primary_sources.geographic_registration_status: Provisional lead only: no original sheet, coordinates or place-name survey control establishes that the44-cell box is on a specific part of this sequence. GAD river spellings also require a controlled crosswalk.
primary_sources.scale_datum: General treaty map scales1:250000 and select1:50000 already established; no identified Muse-reach sheet or datum inspected.
primary_sources.limit: ArticleX protocol maps replace treaty maps; ArticleVIII course-change rule requires applicable agreement evidence. Neither a modern channel nor the present metadata envelope independently assigns these cells.

concrete_new_findings: 44 candidates are confined to one tight eastern box, not spread across the three-child parent; the retained source list is entirely Myanmar administrative sources.
The2019 GAD aggregation has additional named towns and63village tracts; the2014 MuSe census has16tracts. A main Muse report cannot be assumed to cover the eastern aggregated source footprint.
The GAD names Wanding/MangHai/Jiegao and specific local streams; treaty ArticleVII2(7) supplies a named MongKo–ManHsing–Nu reach to investigate only after a location/control crosswalk.
